name: President's House
use: Official residence of the UNH president; events for visitors, alumni, donors and students; interior not public
architect: Specifications by Randlett & Griffin; contractor Walter H. Sargent; financed by Walter M. Parker
style: Neoclassical, mixing Federal and Greek Revival features

facts.text: Replaced the wooden Mathes House, which burned in September 1903 just before President Gibbs's family was to move in.
Walter Parker of Manchester built it at his own expense; the trustees bought it outright in 1905 for $5,500.
Landscape architect Bremer W. Pond drew a planting plan for the grounds in 1925, much of which remains.
Its front wrap-around porch was removed; otherwise there have been few structural changes.

verdict: The president's 1905 Neoclassical brick residence on Garrison Avenue, built after its wooden predecessor burned; little changed but for a lost porch.
notes: Fire date conflict: the archives say Sunday, Sept. 20, 1903; Clio says Sept. 25, 1903. Clio says it is valued at $1.6M. Address: 2 Garrison Ave. No licensed modern photo found; ref-01 is a 1960 archives photo in snow. No interior information (private).
judgeNotes: Archives photo shows a handsome house (exterior 6, one below the old run: a fine house, not a set piece) with bays and a Palladian dormer; interior private and undocumented.
